 Vienna SF previews and predictions: Alcaraz vs. Medvedev, Zverev vs. De Minaur 
 October 30, 2026 
 Ricky 
 Match previews 
 5 
 Four of the top five seeds have advanced in Vienna, making for a blockbuster semifinal lineup on Saturday. Carlos Alcaraz is going up against Daniil Medvedev, while Alexander Zverev faces Alex de Minaur. 
 (3) Daniil Medvedev vs. (2) Carlos Alcaraz
Alcaraz and Medvedev will be squaring off for the 10th time in their careers when they battle on Saturday for a place in the championship match of the Erste Bank Open . The head-to-head series stands at 6-3 in favor of Alcaraz, who has won four of their last five encounters and won their only previous indoor hard-court contest 6-4, 6-4 at the 2023 Nitto ATP Finals. However, Medvedev won their most recent meeting 6-3, 7-6(3) in the semis of the Indian Wells Masters earlier this season.
Whereas just about everyone else has won themselves out coming down the stretch of a long season, Alcaraz is well rested as a result of his four-month layoff earlier in the year and looks poised to finish 2026 strong. The third-ranked Spaniard already owns one title this fall (Tokyo) and may be in line for another following Vienna victories over Karen Khachanov, Nikoloz Basilashvili, and Tommy Paul. Medvedev is one of those guys who has played a ton of matches, but he has not yet hit the wall. The fifth-ranked Russian is 18-2 since the U.S. Open with titles in Hangzhou and Almaty followed by wins this week at the expense of Daniel Merida, Cameron Norrie, and Adrian Mannarino. Medvedev clinched his place in Turin on Friday, so it would be no surprise if he finally runs out of gas in the semis — especially against the toughest opponent he has faced during this hot streak.
 Pick: Alcaraz in 2

 (1) Alexander Zverev vs. (5) Alex de Minaur
De Minaur is still trying to secure his berth in the year-end championship, and this week could not be going much better for him. The world No. 10 has advanced in Vienna with defeats of Tomas Machac, Learner Tien, and Matteo Berrettini, while fellow Turin contenders Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Frances Tiafoe, Rafael Jodar, and Novak Djokovic have already exited their respective events.
Up next for De Minaur on Saturday is a 14th showdown against Zverev, who leads the head-to-head series 9-4 — including 8-0 in traditional tournament competition. That’s right; all four of the Australian’s victories have come in team events. The second-ranked German, who has guaranteed a climb to No. 1 for the first time in his career on Monday, saved four match points against Martin Landaluce in the Vienna first round and then made much quicker work of Tallon Griekspoor and Arthur Fery. With the conditions also favoring Zverev, this should be mostly one-way traffic for the top seed.
 Pick: Zverev in 2
